perturbation_model.construction: white noise smoothed by a Gaussian kernel (scipy.ndimage.gaussian_filter), renormalized to unit variance, scaled pointwise by the crop's _ERR raster magnitude
perturbation_model.correlation_length_note: Not calibrated. Barker et al. 2023 Sec. 3 identify effective resolution as the primary factor in the error; PGDA product 90 publishes LDEM_*_ADJ_EFFRES.TIF, a candidate basis for a physically motivated correlation length (not yet used).
perturbation_model.error_interpretation: RESOLVED (2026-11-16) against the primary source: Barker et al. 2023 (PSJ 4, 183; DOI 10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1), Section 3, accepted manuscript at https://ntrs.nasa.gov/citations/20230014419. The _ERR maps are RMS height errors estimated from an ensemble of 'clone' LDEMs (fractal terrain + LOLA range and geolocation errors, re-gridded as the nominal LDEM), and represent 'the uncertainty in the LDEM gridded height ... relative to the true average height ... within each pixel'. An RMS error from a zero-mean clone ensemble is treated here as a Gaussian 1-sigma per-pixel magnitude. Remaining approximations: the Gaussian shape and the spatial correlation (see correlation length).

vertical_datum_caveat: The adjusted LOLA DEM's exact vertical offset/scaling relative to the 1,737,400 m reference sphere is not formally confirmed (Barker et al. 2023, Planet. Sci. J. 4, 183, DOI 10.3847/PSJ/acf3e1 was not reachable from this environment). This does not affect sigma directly (sigma is a spread statistic, invariant to a constant vertical offset), but is recorded here as an outstanding scientific caveat on the underlying DEM.
